story: Every morning for forty years, Grandma Hoa opened her tiny tea house by the lake in Hanoi and poured two cups: one for herself, one for her husband who used to sit by the window. Her granddaughter Lan visits on a rainy day and asks why. Grandma tells her about the first morning they met, when he spilled tea on her book of poems. Lan sits in the window seat and drinks the second cup. For the first time in years, Grandma laughs.

bible.title: Two Cups at Dawn
bible.logline: A grandmother's forty-year ritual of pouring two teas becomes a bridge for her granddaughter to meet the grandfather she never knew.

cast.name: Grandma Hoa
cast.look: Elderly Vietnamese woman, small rounded stature, silver hair in a neat bun, wearing a muted teal áo dài with frog-button closures. Signature detail: a smooth jade bangle on her left wrist that catches the light.

cast.name: Lan
cast.look: Girl of about ten, round face with a short bob haircut held by a red star-shaped hair clip. Yellow cotton shirt, dark shorts, bare feet. Signature detail: the red star clip always slightly askew.

cast.name: Grandfather (memory)
cast.look: Younger man, tall with gentle eyes, white cotton shirt sleeves rolled to elbows, dark trousers. Signature detail: right thumb stained with black ink from calligraphy.

cast.name: Tea House
cast.look: Tiny wooden structure on stilts over a lake, curved roof with terracotta tiles, sliding paper screens glowing from within. Lanterns hang under eaves. Interior: low lacquered table, built-in window seat facing water, shelves of jars.

cast.name: Window Seat
cast.look: Built-in wooden bench under a wide window, cushioned with faded floral fabric in sage and rose, lacquered frame worn smooth by decades of elbows.

cast.name: Two Tea Cups
cast.look: Matching ceramic cups, pale celadon glaze with subtle crackle pattern. One cup has a tiny chip on its rim — the husband's cup. Steam curls from both.

cast.name: Poem Book
cast.look: Small cloth-bound notebook, indigo cover softened by time, yellowed pages. A tea stain blooms on the first page like a dark flower.

shots.description: Early morning, cold rain mist over the lake. The tea house sits on stilts, lanterns glowing behind paper screens. Through the screens Grandma Hoa is visible at the low table, pouring tea into two cups. Steam rises.
shots.dialogue: Forty years, two cups, every dawn.
shots.speaker: Narrator

shots.description: Interior, warm lantern light. Grandma places the second cup on the window seat cushion, pauses, and touches the chipped rim with her thumb. The jade bangle catches the glow.
shots.dialogue: One for him, one for me.
shots.speaker: grandma

shots.description: Lan enters shaking rain from a clear umbrella, framed over Grandma's shoulder. Water drips from the umbrella rim. Lan's red star clip is askew. She looks at the two cups, curious.
shots.speaker: lan

shots.description: Golden dusk memory hue. Same tea house, brighter. Young Grandma sits at the window seat reading the indigo poem book. Young Husband approaches with two cups, trips on the threshold, tea arcs and splashes across the open pages.
shots.speaker: husband

shots.description: Tea stain blooming on the poem page like ink blossom. Young Grandma's hand covers his ink-stained thumb. Both faces tilt up, laughing silently. Lantern light paints them gold.
shots.speaker: grandma

shots.description: Present interior, rainy grey light. Lan climbs onto the window seat, picks up the chipped cup, sips. Grandma watches from the table, hands folded, eyes wide with surprise.
shots.speaker: lan

shots.description: Grandma's face: crinkles deepen at the eyes, mouth opens in a silent laugh — the first in years. Warmth floods the lantern light on her cheeks. The jade bangle glints.
Golden dusk returns. Exterior wide shot of tea house on the lake, lanterns lit, water rippling gently. Through the window the two cups sit side by side on the low table, steam merging.
shots.speaker: Narrator

continuity: Lan's red star hair clip is described as 'slightly askew' in both Bible and Shot 3, maintaining consistency.
The chipped rim on the husband's cup is explicitly noted in Bible and confirmed in Shot 2 (thumb touching it) and Shot 6 (Lan picks it up).
The jade bangle on Grandma's wrist is consistently highlighted as catching light in Bible and Shots 2 and 7.
The tea stain on the poem-book's first page is described identically ('blooms like a dark flower') in Bible and Shot 4.
The window seat's cushion color (sage and rose floral fabric) is not contradicted in any shot; implied by context but not visually detailed in shots.
The setting transitions from rainy morning (Shot 1) to golden dusk memory (Shot 4) to present rainy grey (Shot 6) are distinct and correctly ordered per narrative intent.
